description: Federal Protection for Family and Medical Leave
whatThisIs: This federal law provides qualifying employees with 12 weeks of unpaid, job-protected leave per year. Two conditions must be met. First, you must have been employed by the company for at least 12 months or worked at least 1,250 hours over the last 12 months. Second, your work location must have 50 or more company employees within 75 miles. This can come into play for chain locations. Most stores do not employ 50 people, but nearby stores may meet that threshold when counted together.
whoItHelps: People and families living in states that don’t have state programs for paid family and medical leave
whatToKnow: Massachusetts has its own state laws for paid family leave. If you're looking for paid family or medical leave, please visit the profile titled “PFML (Paid Family and Medical Leave)”.

FMLA applies to people who need time off for the birth of a child, the placement of a child for adoption, the care of a family member with a serious medical condition, or their own serious medical condition.

Because this is a federal law and not a state or federal program, there is no application process. If you're eligible, you can request time off directly from your employer. Depending on the reason, your employer can request certification from a health care provider. However, you do not have to disclose your health condition. See the Employee Rights pamphlet for more information about how requests for leave and certification work.
name: Family and Medical Leave (FMLA)
